description: Word has gone down Sprocket Row that No. 9's Boiler is lit again, and your neighbours on the Row have begun to find reasons to stop at your window. They have not come to welcome you. Since the summer the Rust Rats have come up out of Rustmoor every night and taken whatever is metal: a pram wheel, a coal scuttle, two bicycle bells, the brass numbers off four doors. The pie shop is out of tins. The Row knows you have been down among the heaps with a spanner, and would like to know what you mean to bring back.

options.label: Promise the Row that next time you are down in Rustmoor, you will find where the rats keep its things, and bring them home.

success.text: The promise goes down the Row the way the news of the Boiler did, gaining detail as it travels. By the pie shop you have found the rats' hoard already. By the corner you have fought something the size of a pony for it, with a spanner, and won. The pie shop sends round two pies to see whether you are eating, and a third for the heaps, with a note: "Not the last, we hope."

options.label: Shut the door, and chalk on it: CLOSED FOR REPAIRS. OPINIONS BY APPOINTMENT.

success.text: The sign is read aloud the length of the Row before the chalk is dry, and improved twice before the hour is out. Nobody calls. But the next day there is a tin of bent nails on your step, saved from somewhere the rats had not reached, and no note. The Row has decided to wait and see. That is as close to a welcome as Sprocket Row gives anyone.
